sec: Polyuria · partial and nephrogenic DI treatment, hypernatremic complication and DI versus SIADH

items.q: Fill up: Partial DI is treated with the three drugs grouped as the 3 C's, namely ______, ______ and ______.
items.exp: Item 2 of the treatment list is partial DI, treated with the 3 C's: chlorpropamide, clofibrate and carbamazepine. (Book p967)

items.q: Three of these drugs belong to the 3 C's used in partial DI. Which one does not?
items.exp: Chlorpromazine is not on the partial DI list; it appears among the 5 C's of drug-induced SIADH, the opposite problem. (Book p967)

items.q: Assess the nephrogenic DI treatment block: I The page states it is difficult to treat and lists a low sodium diet. II Thiazides are the drug of choice because they raise GFR, and amiloride is reserved for lithium-induced DI.
items.exp: Low sodium diet, thiazides as DOC with a fall in GFR and amiloride as DOC for lithium-induced DI are all listed; the thiazide note says reduced GFR, not increased. (Book p967)

items.q: A 44-year-old on long-term lithium has nephrogenic DI with a 24-hour urine of 6 L. Per this page, which drug is the documented drug of choice?
items.exp: Amiloride is labelled the DOC for lithium-induced DI, alongside a low sodium diet and thiazides for nephrogenic DI generally. (Book p967)

items.q: All of the following appear in the management line for nephrogenic DI EXCEPT:
opts: A low sodium diet as a baseline measure
Thiazides entered as the drug of choice
items.exp: The three listed measures are a low sodium diet, thiazides as DOC through a reduced GFR and amiloride for lithium-induced DI; intranasal desmopressin is the treatment of central DI. (Book p967)

items.q: For the hypernatremic complication of DI, by how much should serum sodium be lowered each day?
items.exp: The Rx line reads a fall in Na+ daily of 8-10 mEq/L. (Book p967)

items.q: Using the deficit formula on this page, what is the free water deficit of a 60 kg man with a serum sodium of 158 mEq/L, rounded to one decimal?
items.exp: 0.6 x 60 x (158 - 140)/140 gives 36 x 0.129, about 4.6 L; half of that, roughly 2.3 L, is replaced on day 1. (Book p967)

items.q: Assess the day-1 replacement instructions: I Either 2 L of 5% dextrose or 4 L of half-normal saline is offered to lower sodium by 8 mEq/L. II Whatever free water remains is given as an intravenous 3% saline infusion.
items.exp: Both regimens are equated at a fall of 8 mEq/L, and 50% of the deficit is replaced on day 1; the remaining free water plus ongoing losses go by nasogastric tube, not 3% saline. (Book p967)

items.q: Fill up: The remaining free water and ongoing losses in a hypernatremic DI patient are given via a ______, and the deficit equation multiplies body weight by the factor ______.
items.exp: The formula is 0.6 x body weight x (Na - 140)/140, and the residual deficit together with ongoing losses is delivered through a nasogastric tube. (Book p967)

items.q: Assess the sodium derangement described across these two pages: I The complication box here records hypernatremia and labels it rare. II The clinical-features list on the previous page records abrupt-onset hyponatremia.
items.exp: Both statements reproduce the pages exactly, and the pair is an internal inconsistency of the source: DI deprives the body of free water, so a rising sodium with an intact thirst mechanism is the expected picture, and hypernatremia is what the complication line treats. (Book p967)

items.q: Match each row of the DI-versus-SIADH table with what is entered in the DI column — 1) Serum osmolality 2) Urine volume 3) Urine osmolality 4) Urine Na+ … A) Single arrow up B) Triple arrow up C) Double arrow down D) Normal
items.exp: The DI column reads serum osmolality up, serum Na up, urine volume triple up, urine osmolality double down and urine Na+ normal; SIADH reverses the first two and doubles urine Na+ up. (Book p967)

items.q: Every parameter below is a row of the DI-versus-SIADH table EXCEPT:
items.exp: The table runs causes, features, behaviour in stalk injury, serum osmolality, serum Na, urine volume, urine osmolality and urine Na+; potassium is not a row, and no dipstick row appears here although the polyuria table on p965 has one. (Book p967)

items.q: Assess the causes and features rows of the table: I Euvolemic is entered as a feature of both DI and SIADH. II The causes row attributes DI to paraneoplastic states and SIADH to trauma or tumour.
items.exp: Both columns carry euvolemia, with polyuria under DI and hyponatremia under SIADH; the causes row assigns trauma or tumour to DI and paraneoplastic states to SIADH, the reverse of statement II. (Book p967)

items.q: According to the stalk-injury row, during which window does SIADH appear?
opts: The intermediate stage, day 4 to day 6 or 11
The early stage, before day 4 or 5
The late stage, beyond day 6 to 11
Continuously from the day of surgery
items.exp: DI occupies the early stage under 4-5 days and the late stage beyond 6-11 days, while SIADH fills the intermediate D4 to D6/11 window. (Book p967)

items.q: On day 9 after a transsphenoidal adenomectomy a patient passes 7 L/day with urine osmolality 110 mOsm/kg and serum sodium 148 mEq/L. Which row of the DI-versus-SIADH table fits best?
opts: DI in the late stage of stalk injury, with raised serum osmolality and doubled urine output
SIADH of the intermediate stage, with euvolemic hyponatremia
Psychogenic polydipsia, with a stimulated copeptin above 3.8 pmol/L
Cerebral salt wasting, with hypovolemia and raised BNP
items.exp: Day 9 sits in the late stage the table gives for DI after stalk injury, and the raised sodium and osmolality with dilute high-volume urine match the DI column, not the low sodium of the SIADH column. (Book p967)

items.q: Fill up: In the DI-versus-SIADH table, urine volume in SIADH is written as ______ or ______, while urine osmolality is ______ in SIADH and ______ in DI.
opts: normal; decreased; doubled up; doubled down
doubled up; normal; doubled down; doubled up
decreased; triple up; doubled down; doubled up
normal; triple up; unchanged; doubled down
items.exp: The SIADH column shows urine volume as normal or decreased with urine osmolality doubled up, opposite the DI column's triple-arrow volume and double-arrow fall in osmolality. (Book p967)
